official.description: The International Visegrad Fund's Visegrad Fellowship Program funds individual short-term in-person stays for scholars, lecturers and researchers who are full-time doctoral students or PhD holders from Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia or Ukraine, at institutions in a V4 country other than their own. Fellows conduct or participate in a concrete research project, hold lectures or seminars, or study materials in a public archive or library, supported by a lump-sum scholarship of EUR 500 per week paid in two instalments.
official.region: Europe (Visegrad region: Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia)
official.program_type: Short-term individual research and teaching mobility fellowship
official.english_requirement: All uploaded application documents must be written in English.

applicant_utility.summary: This fellowship suits V4 and Ukrainian doctoral researchers who already have a host contact, because the money is a flat EUR 500 per week and the length you propose sets your budget: a 10-week stay pays EUR 5,000, a 2-week stay pays EUR 1,000. Applications run on rolling terms from January to May and September to November while capacity lasts, and the current fixed call has a hard 12:00 noon cut-off on 30 November 2026. The Fund warns that capacity was exceeded in the previous term, so leaving the submission to the final days of the window is the single biggest risk.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Full-time PhD students and recent PhD holders from Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia or Ukraine who already have an archive, seminar or research project agreed with a host institution in another V4 country.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure a signed or stamped invitation letter from the host institution that fixes the exact dates, a timetable and the intended outcomes before starting the form
Line up a recommendation letter from your home institution, or from a relevant expert if you are not currently affiliated
Draft a research plan in which the number of requested weeks (2-10) is explicitly justified
Translate every document into English before uploading; there is no certified-translation route for this programme
Submit early in the September-November window rather than in the closing days, since the Fund stops accepting once capacity is exceeded
common_rejection_risks: Host institution located in the applicant's own country of citizenship or residence - the rule is absolute
Invitation letter missing the timetable, concrete nature or intended outcomes the Fund expects
Requested length not convincingly justified in both the application and the invitation document
No recommendation letter because an unaffiliated applicant did not arrange a relevant expert as referee
Reapplying within the same term after a rejection, which the Fund explicitly discourages
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The EUR 500 per week is a lump sum with no itemisation, so travel to the host country, accommodation, insurance and any tuition or bench fees must be funded from the fellow's own resources; the Fund publishes no separate allowance for these.
document_audit: Every upload must be in English; unlike the Scholarship Program, no sworn-translation alternative is offered
The invitation letter must be signed or stamped by the host institution - an email from an individual academic is not the accepted form
Proof of doctoral status must be a scanned diploma or enrolment proof, not a CV entry
The recommendation letter must come from the affiliated home institution, or a relevant expert if the applicant has no affiliation
alerts: The Fund states capacities were exceeded in the previous term, so the call can stop accepting applications once capacity is reached
Candidates should avoid reapplying within the same term (January-May or September-November) regardless of outcome; repeat support is possible only in exceptional, justified cases
Remote research or lectures are granted only in exceptional cases of limited mobility and must be justified in both the application and the invitation document
The 20% second instalment arrives only after the first 80%, so plan cash flow for the whole stay in advance
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in My Visegrad, complete the electronic form, upload the four English-language documents, and submit before the 30 November 2026 noon deadline; the award is then paid in two instalments, 80% followed by 20%.

official.tuition_coverage_note: Official FAQ: tuition fees are 'Not directly' covered. Host institutions receive 2,000 EUR per semester per scholar; for master's studies this covers tuition or administrative costs, and excess fees are the scholar's responsibility. For post-master's studies the lump sum covers institutional hosting expenses.

official.application_route: Online application through My Visegrad, submitted before 15 April 2027 at 12:00 (noon); the system opens roughly 45 days before the deadline.
official.study_mode: Full-time (attendance scholarship - the scholar is expected to be at the host institution for the entire period)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to citizens of Czechia, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia, and of Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, Northern Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine. The country of the applicant's citizenship must differ from the country of the host institution, previous university studies must have been completed in another country, and the host must be more than 150 km from the current university/employer or permanent residence.
official.international_eligibility: Restricted to citizens of the Visegrad countries and the Eastern Partnership/Western Balkans countries listed above; applicants of other nationalities are not eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All disciplines, in any language; the application form offers 25 disciplines. Bachelor-level funding is limited to the Intra-V4 scheme for citizens of one V4 country studying in another; Eastern Partnership and Western Balkans citizens can access only master's or post-master's programmes. The host must be an accredited higher-education institution or an institute of a science academy.
official.research_requirement: Post-master's applicants must attach a letter of acceptance with a detailed working plan; no separate research proposal is required at master's level.
official.duration: 1-2 semesters for full-time master's level studies or full-time post-master's studies/research
official.description: The International Visegrad Fund's Visegrad Scholarship Program supports Master's and post-Master's students and researchers in all disciplines and in any language for up to two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe. The support amounts to EUR 3,500 per semester for the scholar plus EUR 2,000 per semester for the host institution, and applicants must cross a border: their citizenship, their previous university studies and their permanent residence must all lie in a different country from the host institution.
official.region: Europe (Central and Eastern Europe: Visegrad countries and the Eastern Partnership/Western Balkans)
official.program_type: Regional mobility scholarship for Master's and post-Master's students and researchers
official.english_requirement: No language certificates are required for study and courses may be taken in the host country's language, but the application form must be filled out in English and uploaded documents must be in English or accompanied by a translation certified by a sworn translator or by the university official.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the Fund's main study and research mobility scholarship: EUR 3,500 per semester goes straight to the scholar and a separate EUR 2,000 per semester goes to the host institution, which for master's study is what pays the tuition. The next call opens 1 January 2027 and closes 15 April 2027 at noon, with results on 31 May 2027, so a September or October 2027 start is the earliest realistic outcome. Eligibility hinges on crossing a border: your citizenship, your previous university and your permanent residence must all sit in a different country from the host, and more than 150 km away.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's and post-Master's students and researchers from the V4 region or the Eastern Partnership/Western Balkans who already hold a degree and want one or two semesters at a host institution in another eligible country.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply to the host university early - a preliminary acceptance letter or proof of application is enough to apply, but the final acceptance letter must be submitted before signing the contract with the Fund
Check the 150 km rule against both your current university or employer and your permanent residence
Prepare transcripts covering at least the last two completed semesters, or a diploma supplement, for master's level
For post-master's level, agree a detailed working plan with the host supervisor to include in the acceptance letter
Arrange sworn-translator or university certification for any document not in English
Budget for tuition or administrative fees above the EUR 2,000 the host institution receives per semester
common_rejection_risks: Previous university studies completed in the same country as the host institution - an absolute bar, including a Czech bachelor's followed by a Czech master's
Host university within 150 km of the applicant's current university, employer or permanent residence
Applying to a host institution in the applicant's own country of citizenship
Missing the 12:00 noon deadline - the Fund states no application past the deadline is accepted under any circumstances
Submitting more than one application, several host institutions or several study programmes in a single round
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition or administrative fees above the EUR 2,000 per semester paid to the host institution, plus travel, accommodation, insurance and visa costs - the Fund states the EUR 3,500 is at the scholar's full disposal and that it cannot cover any additional costs.
document_audit: Documents must be in English or accompanied by a translation certified by a sworn translator or by the university official

Master's applicants need transcripts of at least the last two completed semesters or a diploma supplement; a single semester suffices only for first-year bachelor's applicants under the Intra-V4 scheme
Post-master's applications must place the detailed working plan inside the acceptance letter rather than as a loose attachment

A preliminary acceptance or proof of application is acceptable at submission, but the final acceptance letter is mandatory before the contract is signed

This is an attendance scholarship - you must physically be at the host institution for the whole supported period
Any concurrent scholarship such as Erasmus must be disclosed; the Fund may withdraw its offer based on individual circumstances
Scholarship money is paid in advance for each 5-month semester, and only after the host university sends written arrival confirmation on letterhead with signature and stamp
Recipients must acknowledge the Fund in scholarly documentation and public events and use its logo
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the online form and uploads in My Visegrad before 15 April 2027 at 12:00; after the end-of-May results the contract is mailed to your permanent address, one signed copy is returned by post, and each semester is paid in advance once the host confirms your arrival on signed and stamped letterhead.
